newsitem.title: LATVIA: RUHRGAS, PREUSSEN PAY FOR MOST OF GAS STAKE.
newsitem.headline: RUHRGAS, PREUSSEN PAY FOR MOST OF GAS STAKE.

text.p: The privatisation agency on Wednesday said the German consortium of Preussen and Ruhrgas which together won a bid to buy 16.25 percent of Latvian Gas has settled for 70 percent of the stake.

Janis Naglis, LPA general director, told a news conference that the consortium has paid 7.87 million lats for the existing shares out of 11.25 million lats due by August 15 and paid in full for a new issue of shares, worth 3.37 million lats.
The sum paid for the existing shares will remain at the disposal of Latvian Gas while the payment for the new issue payment goes into the state's coffers, Naglis said.
Gazprom won the bid for another 16.25 percent and has to pay for the shares.
"We hope Russia's Gazprom will cope with its current problems and settle its part of the payment by the August deadline," Naglis said.
He said that Gazprom still had to convince two more institutions before applying to the Russian central bank to make an investment abroad.
